recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. Further edits would be redundant and could create maintenance drift; revisit only if FHIR-I intentionally changes the empty-string policy.
issue_request: FHIR-17639 was Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification for STU3. It asked to resolve the mismatch where JSON/XML already prohibited empty string primitive values while the string datatype regex and validator behavior appeared to allow them; the final decision kept empty strings unsupported, added a whitespace-only string note, and required validator rejection of empty primitive values.
initial_application: Commit f8e58880f9ee09717f279992dbbaebce6a1601d7 explicitly applied GF#17639 by adding the datatype note and validator examples/tests, including invalid empty valueString and valueMarkdown values. The current source retains the note and also states that XML attributes and JSON primitive properties are never zero length.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini keeps the datatype and primitive sources in build scope via the type-page fallback to datatypes.html and the active PrimitiveType infrastructure entry. JSON and XML representation pages still prohibit empty string property values and attributes. Later FHIR-32800 and FHIR-40563 refined string serialization and regex behavior without reversing the empty-string prohibition; commit b4c3af0a97 changed string and markdown regexes to ^[\s\S]+$, which accepts any non-empty content while rejecting empty values. Quoted Zulip and Confluence searches found no FHIR-17639-specific contrary discussion, and a 2026 FHIR-I openEHR mapping minutes page describes FHIR as rejecting empty-string primitives.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already conveys the FHIR-17639 decision: empty strings remain invalid, omitted elements represent missing values, whitespace-only strings are allowed but warned against, and the primitive regex source requires at least one character.
